you.label: You
you.blurb: Yours alone; changes affect nobody else.

workspace.label: Workspace
workspace.blurb: Policy for everyone in the workspace.

account.label: Account
account.title: Who you are, and where you are signed in
account.description: Your profile and photo, how you appear in this workspace, your sign-in details, and every browser that currently holds a session.

appearance.label: Appearance
appearance.title: How the app looks, and how it answers you
appearance.description: Five controls, not eleven: four for the screen, one for how the assistant answers. Board colours in a mindmap are part of the map, not the theme.

shortcuts.label: Shortcuts
shortcuts.title: What the keyboard does
shortcuts.description: Every command, its keys, and a place to change them. Yours alone; the mindmap editor keeps its own map while a map is open.

people.label: People and access
people.title: Who is in the workspace, and what they can see
people.description: Members and their roles, invitations and join links, groups, custom roles, and the audit log. Who can open a folder is set on the folder itself; roles decide everything else.

company.label: Company profile
company.title: What your sources can prove
company.description: Read from the sources written by or about your company, each fact with the excerpt that proves it. Agents cite it for company context and Proposals drafts from it. Sources about someone else are set aside, and you can overrule that.

byok.label: Bring your own keys
byok.title: Bring your own keys
byok.description: Your own provider account for the workspace's AI, and your own key for embeddings. Both are optional: anything left empty runs on the server's keys.

models.label: Models and routes
models.title: Which model serves each kind of request
models.description: The server's default models and routes, set in its configuration file and shown here read-only. A workspace that brings its own API key runs on that instead.

agents.label: Agents and autonomy
agents.blurb: The roster, and what it may do
agents.title: Who shows up to a meeting, and how much they may do alone
agents.description: Each agent is a seat in a meeting: a name, a role, standing instructions, and a level of autonomy. Agents can run in this app or on another machine you connect.

integrations.label: Integrations
integrations.title: What this workspace connects to
integrations.description: Workspace connections to Drive, Slack and GitHub; Slack mirroring for meetings; and the hub that remote agent machines dial into. All optional and independent.

usage.label: Usage and costs
usage.title: What the workspace is spending
usage.description: Every AI model call the workspace made and what it cost, then the token balance and what has been drawing on it. The numbers exist to inform the two settings on this page.

archive.label: Archive and retention
archive.title: What has been put away, and when it goes for good
archive.description: Trashed maps and artifacts, retired agents and archived channels, with restore and permanent delete. The retention window decides what the trash empties on its own.

privacy.label: Data and privacy
privacy.title: What leaves this deployment, and what stays
privacy.description: Which outside services see document text, which see only metadata, what is kept and for how long. Read this before trusting the app with something sensitive.

labs.label: Labs
labs.title: Features that are not finished
labs.description: Each one says honestly what it does today. Off by default; turning one on affects the whole workspace.

theme.label: Theme
theme.description: Light, dark, or whatever your system is using.

density.label: Density
density.description: How much fits on screen. Compact tightens spacing and type in lists.

reducedMotion.label: Motion
reducedMotion.description: Animations and transitions across the app.

responseStyle.label: Answer style of the default assistant
responseStyle.description: How Launchstack answers when no agent is picked in the composer. An agent brings its own style, so this never applies to one.

bindings.label: Keyboard shortcuts
bindings.description: Which keys run which commands. Yours alone; other members keep their own.

productAnalytics.label: Product analytics
productAnalytics.description: Whether page views from your browser count toward the hosted product's usage analytics. Off the hosted service nothing is sent regardless.

auditRetentionDays.label: Keep audit events for
auditRetentionDays.description: How long the audit log is kept.
auditRetentionDays.consequence: Older events are deleted. Export a CSV first if you need a permanent copy.

defaultAutonomy.label: Default autonomy for agents
defaultAutonomy.description: How much an agent with no level of its own may do unattended. Each agent can be set lower or higher on its card.
defaultAutonomy.consequence: Lowering this can stop meetings from mirroring to Slack or running on their own until the room's agents are raised again.

pricePerMillionTokens.label: Price per million tokens
pricePerMillionTokens.description: What a million ledger tokens cost you, in your currency. Used only to estimate spend on this page; leave 0 to show tokens alone.

lowBalanceThreshold.label: Low balance warning
lowBalanceThreshold.description: The balance below which this page and the balance chip warn.

trashDays.label: Empty the trash after
trashDays.description: Trashed maps and artifacts older than this are removed for good.
trashDays.consequence: Applied the next time the archive is opened. A removed item cannot be restored.

predictiveGaps.label: Predictive gaps
predictiveGaps.description: Lists missing exhibits, schedules and compliance gaps across your documents. The analysis exists; the screen that shows it does not yet, so this only surfaces the entry in the palette.

row.permissionReason: Changing this takes a role with “{permission}”.
row.setByLeft: Set {when} by someone who has left

answerStyle.ownChoice: Your own choice, {label}, still applies to your chats. <link>Change it under Appearance</link>.

display.title: Display
display.description: Applied to this browser as soon as you change it, and remembered for you everywhere you sign in.

answers.title: Answers
answers.description: How Launchstack answers you in chat when no agent is picked. Yours alone: nobody else's answers change.

archive.restored: Restored {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
archive.deleted: Deleted {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} for good

retention.description: What the trash empties on its own. Retired agents and archived channels are never removed automatically.

putAway.title: Put away
putAway.description: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}. Restore puts a thing back where it was; delete is for good.

archive.notDeletable: Agents and channels cannot be deleted for good.

confirm.restoreBody: Each item goes back to where it was.

offReasons.disabled: The assistant server is turned off on this LaunchStack server. Ask whoever runs it to turn it on (MCP_SERVER_ENABLED).
offReasons.noBaseUrl: This LaunchStack server doesn't know its own web address, so assistants can't sign in. Ask whoever runs it to set BETTER_AUTH_URL.
offReasons.insecureBaseUrl: Assistants can only sign in to a LaunchStack server reached over HTTPS. This one's address is plain HTTP; ask whoever runs it to serve it over HTTPS.

assistants.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text and copy it yourself.
assistants.signInPick: Sign in to LaunchStack and pick this workspace.

claude.step1: In Claude (claude.ai or the desktop app), open <menu>Customize › Connectors › Add custom connector</menu> and paste the server URL.
claude.step2: Choose <menu>Sign in now</menu>, and for the OAuth client pick <menu>Use Claude''s published identity</menu> (<menu>Register automatically</menu> also works).
claude.note1: Free plans can add one custom connector. On Team and Enterprise, an Owner first adds it under <menu>Organization settings › Connectors › Add › Custom</menu>; then each member connects from Customize › Connectors.
claude.note2: For a script or a shared setup, choose No sign-in and add the request header {header} instead. Claude still marks that option beta for some organizations.

chatgpt.step1: In ChatGPT, open <menu>Settings › Apps & Connectors › Advanced settings</menu> and turn on <menu>Developer mode</menu>.
chatgpt.step2: Create a connector named LaunchStack with the server URL, and choose OAuth for authentication.
chatgpt.note: Which plans get developer mode, and whether a workspace admin has to turn it on and publish the connector, is set by OpenAI and changes; check OpenAI’s developer-mode help page for your plan.

gemini.step1Admin: Create an OAuth client in Settings › Integrations, under OAuth clients for assistants. It gives you a client ID and secret, and the URLs and scopes to paste.
gemini.step1Member: A LaunchStack admin creates an OAuth client in Settings › Integrations. It gives them a client ID and secret, and the URLs and scopes to paste.
gemini.step2: A Google Cloud admin opens <menu>Gemini Enterprise › Data stores › Create data store › Custom MCP Server</menu>, chooses OAuth 2.0, pastes the server URL, authorization URL, token URL, client ID, client secret and scopes, and ticks <menu>Enable PKCE Support</menu>. Without PKCE, LaunchStack refuses the sign-in.
gemini.step3: Each person then signs in to LaunchStack from Gemini and picks this workspace.
gemini.note: Google blocks custom MCP data stores by default: an organization policy admin has to override that policy and allow LaunchStack’s domain as an egress destination. Whoever creates the data store needs the Discovery Engine Editor role.

claudeCode.note: Then run /mcp in Claude Code, choose launchstack and sign in.

codex.note: The second command opens your browser to sign in.

geminiCli.note: Then run /mcp auth launchstack in Gemini CLI to sign in.

api.intro: Create an access key below and send it with every request to the server URL:
api.note: The server speaks MCP over streamable HTTP. Keys never expire; revoke them here.

keyCreated.title: Copy your key now
keyCreated.description: You won't see it again. If you lose it, revoke it and create another.

createKey.title: Create an access key
createKey.description: The key acts as you, in this workspace only. Anyone who has it can do what you choose here.
createKey.nameHint: So you can tell your keys apart, e.g. “Nightly export script”.
createKey.readDetail: Search the workspace and open the documents you can see.
createKey.writeDetail: Also save an assistant's conversation into the workspace as a document.
createKey.noSave: Saving conversations needs permission to add documents, which your role doesn't include.

section.title: Assistants (MCP)
section.description: Let Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini search this workspace and save conversations into it. Each connection acts as you, in this workspace only, and sees only what you can.

assistants.pasteIt: Paste it into the assistant. It sends you here to sign in and asks which workspace to use.

connected.title: Connected assistants
connected.description: Assistants you have signed in to this workspace. Revoking one cuts it off at its next request; what it already saved stays.

keys.title: Access keys
keys.description: For scripts, API calls and command-line tools that can't sign in through a browser. A key acts as you, in this workspace only.

confirm.keyBody: Anything using this key stops working at its next request. This can't be undone.
confirm.connectionBody: It loses access to this workspace at its next request. Conversations it already saved stay. You can connect it again any time.

drive.description: Link PDFs and Word documents to Google Drive so they can be edited with real tools — Google Docs for Word files, any Drive app or Drive for Desktop for PDFs. Settled edits sync back as document versions.
drive.setup: Set GOOGLE_DOCS_EDITING_ENABLED=true, GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET (a GCP OAuth client with the drive.file scope) to enable this feature.
drive.connectedAs: Connected as {email}. Linked files live in this account''s My Drive.
drive.notConnected: No Google account is connected for this workspace yet.
drive.confirmTitle: Disconnect Google Drive from this workspace?
drive.confirmBody: Its Google account is unlinked. You can connect it again from this page.

slackCommands.takeover: Pause the agents and take the floor, optionally in an agent's seat
slackCommands.release: Hand control back to the agents
slackCommands.run: Let the agents take up to three more turns
slackCommands.end: Close the meeting and produce minutes
slackCommands.help: Post the command reference into the channel

connections.title: Workspace connections
connections.description: Accounts this workspace has connected. Connecting happens in the documents workspace under Add source → Connect; tokens are encrypted at rest and never leave the server.
connections.noneAvailable: Nothing connected yet. Available on this server: {list}.
connections.noClients: No provider OAuth clients are configured. Set the client-id / client-secret pairs described in .env.example (Workspace connections block) plus EMBEDDING_SECRETS_KEY.
connections.confirmBody: The connection is removed and its access revoked. To connect again, use Add source → Connect.

slack.description: Hold a meeting in a real Slack channel. Agent turns are posted there, and anything a person writes back lands in the same transcript.
slack.postOn: Meeting turns are mirrored into the linked channel.
slack.postOff: Set SLACK_BOT_TOKEN with chat:write on a Slack app installed to your workspace.
slack.receiveOn: Messages people write in Slack are added to the meeting, including the controls below.
slack.receiveOff: Set SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET so inbound Events API deliveries can be verified.

setup.title: Slack app setup
setup.description: Two things to configure on the Slack side, once per workspace.
setup.step2: Subscribe to message.channels, plus message.groups for private channels.
setup.step3: Invite the bot to the channel, then paste that channel id when starting a meeting.

controls.title: In-channel controls
controls.description: What someone can type in Slack to steer a running meeting. Prefixed with ! rather than / so no extra Slack app configuration is needed.

hub.title: Meeting hub
hub.description: The endpoint agent worker machines dial into. Which machines are attached, and how to connect one, lives under Agents & nodes.
hub.off: Set COLLAB_HUB_SECRET to let worker machines register. Without it, every agent runs in this process.

openRouter.connectedActive: OpenRouter is connected, and this workspace uses it.
openRouter.connected: OpenRouter is connected. Choose a model to switch your workspace over.
openRouter.denied: OpenRouter sign-in was cancelled. Nothing changed.

openRouter.error: Couldn't connect OpenRouter. Try again, or use an API key instead.

embedding.title: Embedding key
embedding.description: Optional. An OpenAI-compatible key for the vectors behind semantic search, sent only to the endpoint it belongs to. Without one, embeddings run on the server's key.

embedding.removed: Removed. Embeddings run on the server's key again.

embedding.serverHint: Leave blank to use the server's key.

labs.title: Experiments
labs.description: Off by default. On for everyone in the workspace once an admin turns one on.

routeBlurb.default: Everything not routed elsewhere: Ask, meetings, drafts.
routeBlurb.fast: Small structured calls: metadata extraction, starters, classification.
routeBlurb.reasoning: Requests that ask for a reasoning effort.

server.title: Server default
server.description: The models this server runs any workspace on that hasn't brought its own. One AI endpoint serves every route; its address and credential stay on the server.
server.usesOwn: This workspace runs on its own model, set up in Bring your own keys, so the server default below isn’t used.
server.ownNoModel: This workspace’s own API key has no model chosen yet, so it still runs on the server default. Choose one in Bring your own keys.
server.fixFile: {error} Fix the file named by CHAT_MODELS_CONFIG and re-read.
server.fileNote: Models are set in the server’s chat model file, named by CHAT_MODELS_CONFIG. Edit that file and restart to change a model; nothing here writes to it.

routes.title: Routes
routes.description: A route is a capability the app asks for. A route with no explicit model inherits default when default can serve it.

declared.title: Declared models
declared.description: What each configured model is declared to do. A preset is a verified catalog entry; an override is the operator's own word, taken as given.

basic.title: In an HTTP Basic header

create.sendsSecret: How the assistant sends the secret

chat.label: Chat and generation
chat.note: Every question, the passages retrieved to answer it, and every generated document go here.

embedding.label: Embeddings
embedding.note: Every chunk of every indexed document is sent to be embedded. Companies with their own key or an Ollama endpoint override this per workspace.

rerank.label: Reranking
rerank.note: Candidate passages for a question are sent to be reordered.

ner.label: Entity extraction
ner.note: Runs only when entity extraction is turned on for a document.

ocr.native: Native PDF extraction only; nothing leaves the server.

transcription.label: Transcription

email.label: Outbound email
email.note: Invitations, password resets and approved campaigns. Never document text.

slack.note: Only meetings that mirror to a channel; the agents' turns are posted there.

drive.note: Only files someone links or creates in Drive; synced back as versions.

notion.note: Reads only the pages picked on Notion's consent screen. Nothing is written to Notion.

secEdgar.label: Investor search
secEdgar.note: Only the words and state typed into Find investors. Never document text.

kept.title: What is kept
kept.description: Retention windows live where they are set; this is the summary.

audit.label: Audit log
audit.detail: Set under People and access. <link>Change it</link>.

trash.label: Trash
trash.detail: Trashed maps and artifacts. Set under Archive and retention. <link>Change it</link>.

credentials.label: Embedding credentials
credentials.detail: Per-workspace keys are encrypted with EMBEDDING_SECRETS_KEY and only ever shown as their last four characters.

choices.title: Your choices
choices.noEffectBody: This instance sends no analytics, so the switch changes nothing until it runs on the hosted service.

profile.usingProfile: Using your profile in this workspace

section.title: Profile
section.loadingDescription: How you appear to the people you work with.
section.description: Yours in every workspace you belong to. A workspace can show a different photo, name or title — see below.

profile.photoHint: JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF or AVIF, up to {mb} MB. You can crop it next.
profile.fullNameHint: Used for sign-in, invitations and the audit trail.
profile.displayNameHint: What people see in lists and chat. Blank uses your full name.
profile.title: Title
profile.timeZoneHint: Lets others see your local time before they message you.
profile.aboutPlaceholder: A line about what you work on.
profile.emailHint: Sign-in email. Ask an admin to re-invite you to change it.

workspaceSection.title: In {workspace}
workspaceSection.description: Show up differently in this workspace only — a client's logo, the name they know you by, your title there. Blank fields use your profile. Other workspaces never see these.

photoDialog.descriptionIn: Only people in {workspace} will see it.
photoDialog.descriptionProfile: Drag to position, zoom to fit. Everyone in your workspaces sees this unless you set one for a workspace.

profilePhoto.prepareFailed: Your browser couldn't prepare the photo.
profilePhoto.position: Photo position. Drag or use the arrow keys to move it, plus and minus to zoom.
profilePhoto.cantOpen: Your browser can't open that file. Try a JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF or AVIF.

shortcuts.conflicts: {count, plural, one {One binding is shared} other {# bindings are shared}} by more than one command. The command lower in the list wins.

commands.title: Commands
commands.description: Click a shortcut to change it, then press the new keys. Backspace removes it. ⌘ on a Mac is Ctrl elsewhere.

elsewhere.title: Elsewhere
elsewhere.description: Some surfaces bring their own keys and are not remapped here.
elsewhere.body: The mindmap editor binds single letters for its tools (V, R, E, T…) and ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z for undo while a map is open. The command palette itself uses ↑ ↓ and ↵.

usage.lowBalance: The balance is below the low-balance warning of {threshold} tokens.

balance.title: Balance
balance.setPrice: Set a price below to estimate spend.

models.title: AI model usage
models.description: Every call this workspace made to an AI model, from every feature, counted from the provider's own report. Separate from the balance below, which only some features draw on.
models.ownEndpoint: {calls} of these calls went to the model endpoint this workspace brought itself. Its own provider bills them.
models.tokens: Model tokens in the last {days} days
models.costPriced: From the price set for each model.
models.costFallback: Models without a set price are counted at {price} per 1M.
models.costPartial: {priced} of {calls} calls have a model price; the rest aren't counted.
models.costNone: No price is set for these models. Set a price below to estimate.
models.nothing: No model calls in this window.

burn.title: Burn by day
burn.description: Tokens drawn from the balance, by what drew them. Hover a day for the breakdown; the table below carries the same numbers.
burn.nothing: Nothing drew on the balance in this window.

pricing.title: Pricing and warnings
pricing.description: The numbers above exist to inform these two.

recent.title: Recent ledger entries
recent.description: The last forty movements on the balance.

default.label: Main model
default.hint: Answers everything not routed elsewhere: Ask, meetings, drafts, background work.

fast.label: Fast
fast.hint: Small structured calls: metadata extraction, starters, classification.

reasoning.label: Reasoning
reasoning.hint: Requests that ask for a reasoning effort. Has to be a reasoning model.

vision.label: Images
vision.hint: Requests that carry an image. Has to be a model that reads images.

anthropic.note: Uses Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible API. A Claude Pro or Max plan can't be used here; it needs an API key.

openrouter.note: One account, hundreds of models, billed to your OpenRouter credits.

custom.label: Other OpenAI-compatible
custom.note: Any server that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions protocol, including one you host.

workspaceModel.testing: Testing {count, plural, one {the model} other {# models}}… each can take up to 45 seconds.
workspaceModel.savedActive: Saved. This workspace's AI now runs on your model.
workspaceModel.savedChoose: Saved. Choose a main model to switch the workspace over.
workspaceModel.disconnected: Disconnected. This workspace is back on the server's default models, and the saved key is deleted.

section.title: API key
section.description: Optional. Run this workspace's AI on your own provider account: chat, drafting, meetings and background work use it, and your provider bills you directly instead of using LaunchStack credits. Without one, the workspace runs on the server's default models.

workspaceModel.checking: Checking for a model of your own…
workspaceModel.intro: OpenRouter asks you to approve a key, then brings you back here to pick a model. An API key works with any provider that offers an OpenAI-compatible API, including a server you host.

confirm.title: Disconnect your own model?
confirm.description: This workspace goes back to the server's default models and the saved key is deleted.

summary.notChosenNote: Connected, but no model is chosen yet, so this workspace still runs on the server default. Choose one under Edit.
summary.offNoImages: Off: the main model doesn't read images
summary.offNoReason: Off: the main model doesn't reason

problems.badId: That doesn't look like a model id. Copy it exactly as your provider lists it, with no spaces.
problems.needsReasoning: Only a reasoning model can take this work. Tick “Reasons step by step”, or leave it empty.
problems.needsVision: Only a model that reads images can take this work. Tick “Reads images”, or leave it empty.

editor.keepEnding: Leave blank to keep the key ending {last4}
editor.keepSaved: Leave blank to keep the saved key
editor.pasteOptional: Paste the key, if your server needs one
editor.keyHintChanged: The address changed, so enter the key for the new address. A saved key is only sent to the address it was saved with.
editor.keyHintStored: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
editor.baseUrlHint: The address of your provider’s OpenAI-compatible API, ending at the path, like /v1.
editor.listedNone: The server listed no models. Type the id instead.
editor.listed: {count} models listed. Pick one as you type, or type any id.
editor.listFailedSuffix: {message} You can still type a model id.
editor.listOptional: Optional: list what your account can reach. Some servers don’t list their models; you can always type an id.
editor.moreModels: Use different models for some work
editor.moreHint: Leave one empty and that work uses the main model.
editor.testHint: Sends each model one short message. Nothing is saved.
editor.modelIdPlaceholder: Model id, exactly as your provider lists it
editor.structuredHint: Structured output (response_format: json_schema). On for most OpenAI, Gemini and OpenRouter models; off for Claude through Anthropic’s compatible API. When it’s off, LaunchStack asks for JSON in the prompt instead.

models.enterAddress: Enter the address of your model endpoint.
models.notWebAddress: That isn't a web address. It should look like https://api.example.com/v1.
models.needsHttps: The address has to start with https://.

models.emptyAnswer: The model answered with nothing. Check that it is a chat model.
models.modelError: The endpoint returned an error for this model. Check the model id and that the key can use it.
models.noSecretsKey: This server can't store API keys yet: whoever runs it needs to set EMBEDDING_SECRETS_KEY.
models.keyForNewAddress: The address changed, so enter the API key for the new address. A saved key is only ever sent to the address it was entered for.
models.keyForThisAddress: Enter the API key for this address. A saved key is only sent to the address it was saved with.
models.notModelId: "{id}" doesn't look like a model id. Copy it exactly as your provider lists it.
